title: Telegram Bot API Getupdates: Free Tools, Real Trade-offs
meta_description: What does Telegram Bot API Getupdates cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source alternatives and…
intro: This is the kind of post The Free Stack exists to write: a practical, no-fluff guide to telegram bot api getupdates, assembled from free tiers, open-source projects and endpoints that ask for no API key at all.

We'll walk through Telegram Bot API, Bluesky At Protocol, Mastodon API, and Measure before you optimize — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Telegram Bot API
paragraphs: Start with the basics. The Telegram Bot API is free, HTTP-based and needs nothing but a token from @BotFather.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? Create a bot in one message, then send and receive messages, create channels, and drive webhooks entirely over plain HTTPS. It is the cheapest 'social media' channel a self-publishing site can own, and this blog posts to it when a token is configured.
No signup wall, no credit card — just a README and some patience.
bullets: Message @BotFather and /newbot to get a token
Optionally set a webhook with setWebhook for incoming events

sections.heading: Bluesky At Protocol
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Bluesky runs on the open AT Protocol, whose public API is free — an account plus an app password is all a bot needs to post.

So what does that look like when you're actually doing it? createSession returns an access token, and app.bsky.feed.post publishes a post. No middleman, no paid 'basic tier' for your own account's posting, and the protocol is openly specified so the implementation is boring in the best way.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.

sections.heading: Mastodon API
paragraphs: Worth spending ten minutes on: Mastodon's API is free and fully documented — any instance lets you register an app and post programmatically.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: Create an app in your instance's developer settings, exchange it for a token, and the REST API handles statuses, follows and search. Because the whole platform is open source and federated, posting to it costs nothing and can point at an instance you run yourself.
Write down what you change and why — your future self will thank you.

sections.heading: Measure before you optimize
paragraphs: Here's the part most people get wrong. You cannot improve what you do not measure, and the measurement tools here are all free.

Which, in day-to-day terms, means: Search console data, a simple counter in your build log, or raw access logs tell you which pages earn their keep. Ten minutes of reading that data is worth more than an hour of guessing, and none of it requires a paid analytics account.
Keep it this simple and you'll be ahead of most tutorials out there.
